svg.text: How a smarli. cover decides where to move
packages/smarli_cover.yaml — contributors publish, one resolver decides, one mover commands
reports its state — if it can
2 · A person commands it in HA
3 · It stops in the wrong place
its own user — not a person
Nothing here commands a cover directly — every arrow is a real event or tracker key; contributors publish, the resolver decides, the mover executes.
A day in the life of one blind
cover.wohnzimmer — same colors as the diagram above, same components in charge
Day-Night is the only contributor right now. It publishes target 100 for
cover.wohnzimmer and calls resolve — no bounds stand against it,
so 100 wins outright. The cover opens.
Shading now stands a bound: cover.wohnzimmer must stay ≤20. Day-
Night's target is still 100, but clamp(100, 0…20) = 20. A single
priority number could never say "cap the ceiling, allow the floor."
A wall-switch press is contextless — no app, no automation. With no
live marker, layer 2 calls it manual and suspends the cover for 30
minutes. At 14:10 the suspension quietly expires — nothing re-asserts
the shaded position. Cancel, not pause.
Shading drops its bound silently — no target — or Day-Night's
21:00 close would get reopened early. It also publishes a one-shot
retract target of 100. With no Day-Night automation at all, this is
the only thing that ever reopens the window again.
Day-Night wants it closed, but the forecast currently matches a
blocked condition. The close is skipped — and nothing is published,
so the schedule can't drift out of sync. It retries every minute and
closes the moment the weather clears.
Home Assistant restarts mid-night. On boot, Day-Night compares what
it last told the resolver against what the schedule wants right now —
not what the cover happens to be doing. Any mismatch forces an
immediate catch-up on the startup trigger.
If the blind is an old Somfy (RTS) model
It never reports what it does. Whether a move by hand is noticed depends on how it is made.
Someone lowers it in the app
The blind sends no state change. But the app's command passes through
Home Assistant, tagged with the person who tapped. The command check
suspends the blind for 30 minutes — the same result as a wall-switch
press on a blind that reports back.
Someone uses the old Somfy remote
The remote talks to the motor directly by radio. Home Assistant never
hears it — no state change, no command. The automation cannot know,
so the next scheduled move happens as planned. Noticing it would
need an extra 433 MHz radio receiver.
If nobody is home and Presence Simulation runs
The simulation replays past moves. From version 7.1, Day-Night leaves its covers alone.
The family leaves — the simulation starts
Day-Night still publishes its targets. For the covers in the simulation,
the resolver records the result but sends no command. The replays come
from the simulation's own user, not from a person, so they never
The family is back — the simulation stops
Every held cover moves to the position the resolver last recorded —
at this hour, closed. Covers outside the simulation were never held.
Older than v7.1: there is no hold, so Day-Night and the simulation
get in each other's way. Upgrade the simulation first.
sensor.smarli_automation_tracker → attributes.data — cover.wohnzimmer, moments apart on the same day above
Real key grammar — CLAUDE.md § State tracking and docs/cover-architecture.md.
"shared" holds anything more than one blueprint touches — intents, resolved positions, suspensions, moving markers.
A per-blueprint namespace like "cover_day_night" only appears once that family writes its own bookkeeping —
here, a brightness instance's stabilizer timestamp.
